nodes.summary: Norwegian Bokmal translation dictionary for the session-review UI, exporting a flat `dict` keyed by the English baseline's message IDs.
nodes.languageNotes: Keys are typed as `keyof typeof en` against the English dictionary (./en), so a missing or misspelled key is a compile-time error.

nodes.name: comment-hover.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a floating 'add comment' button that tracks the hovered diff line and triggers line-comment selection, synced via a requestAnimationFrame loop.

nodes.name: createHoverCommentUtility
nodes.summary: Creates and wires a floating comment button that follows the hovered diff line, syncing position every animation frame and opening line-comment selection on click or Enter/Space.

nodes.name: commented-lines.ts
nodes.summary: Marks already-commented diff and file lines in the rendered viewer by setting data-comment-selected attributes over the line ranges covered by each comment.

nodes.name: markCommentedDiffLines
nodes.summary: Applies data-comment-selected to the rendered diff rows spanned by each comment range, resolving start/end to unified or split row indices and merging overlapping comment indices.

nodes.name: markCommentedFileLines
nodes.summary: Applies data-comment-selected to whole-file line rows covered by comment ranges, clamping ranges to the file's rendered lines and merging annotation indices.

nodes.name: diff-selection.ts
nodes.summary: Helpers that map DOM positions inside rendered diffs to logical diff line/side indices and normalize browser selections so they snap to whole diff lines.

nodes.name: findDiffSide
nodes.summary: Determines whether a DOM node sits on the before or after side of a split diff by walking up to the nearest side container element.

nodes.name: diffLineIndex
nodes.summary: Parses a diff row's comma-separated line-index attribute into numeric line indices, filtering out non-numeric entries.

nodes.name: diffRowIndex
nodes.summary: Finds the rendered row index for a logical diff line (and side) by querying data-line/data-alt-line attributes and matching the diff side.

nodes.name: fixDiffSelection
nodes.summary: Normalizes a browser selection inside a diff so the anchor/focus collapse to whole line rows, producing a corrected SelectedLineRange for line commenting.

nodes.name: file-find.ts
nodes.summary: Implements in-file find (Ctrl/Cmd+F) for the pierre viewers: scans rendered line text with a TreeWalker, highlights matches via the CSS Custom Highlight API with an overlay fallback, and manages match navigation and shortcuts across multiple find hosts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the CSS Custom Highlight API (::highlight(opencode-find)) when available and falls back to manually positioned overlay rectangles; match state lives in a SolidJS store and hosts are tracked in a module-level Set so one global shortcut listener can route to the active viewer.

nodes.name: installShortcuts
nodes.summary: Installs a one-time global keydown listener that routes Ctrl/Cmd+F (and F3/Enter navigation) to the currently active find host, skipping editable targets.

nodes.name: createFileFind
nodes.summary: Builds a file-find controller for one viewer: lazily scans rendered line text for query matches, drives find-bar state and positioning, applies highlights via the Highlight API or an overlay fallback, keeps overlay rects synced to scroll, and exposes open/close/focus/next.

nodes.name: file-runtime.ts
nodes.summary: Runtime glue for pierre viewer custom elements: locates the shadow-DOM host/root, syncs the color-scheme attribute with system mode, and waits for shadow content to be ready before firing onRendered.

nodes.name: applyViewerScheme
nodes.summary: Propagates the current color-scheme mode onto the pierre viewer host element as a data-color-scheme attribute (removing it for light mode).

nodes.name: observeViewerScheme
nodes.summary: Keeps the viewer host's color-scheme attribute in sync with system dark-mode changes via a media-query listener, disconnecting the monitor when the host disappears.

nodes.name: notifyShadowReady
nodes.summary: Waits until a viewer's shadow DOM content is ready (rAF polling plus a MutationObserver fallback), then fires onReady exactly once — handling already-rendered, late-mounting, and dynamically-mutating roots.

nodes.name: file-selection.ts
nodes.summary: Reads the user's text selection inside a shadow DOM and converts it into logical file/diff line ranges plus a before/after side for line commenting.

nodes.name: findFileLineNumber
nodes.summary: Extracts the whole-file line number for a DOM node from its nearest data-line ancestor element.

nodes.name: findDiffLineNumber
nodes.summary: Extracts before/after diff line numbers for a DOM node from its nearest data-diff-line ancestor element.

nodes.name: readShadowLineSelection
nodes.summary: Reads the current selection inside a shadow root (using getComposedRanges when available), maps anchor/focus nodes to file/diff line numbers and sides, and returns a normalized SelectedLineRange.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the newer Selection.getComposedRanges({ shadowRoots }) API to read selections across shadow boundaries, falling back to window.getSelection().getRangeAt.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Public surface of the @pierre/diffs wrapper: defines DiffProps, a large unsafeCSS block theming the diff shadow DOM with OpenCode design tokens, default diff options, and diff typography style variables.
nodes.languageNotes: unsafeCSS is injected into the @pierre/diffs shadow root; overrides are expressed with modern CSS (color-mix(), light-dark(), relative rgb() syntax) layered over design-token CSS variables, with dark-scheme fixes under :host([data-color-scheme='dark']).

nodes.name: createDefaultOptions
nodes.summary: Builds the default @pierre/diffs FileDiffOptions for OpenCode (OpenCode theme, wrap overflow, bar indicators, 20-line expansion, hidden file header), including the injected unsafeCSS and split-aware word-diff settings.

nodes.name: media.ts
nodes.summary: Decodes media file content for the session review: normalizes MIME types, classifies image/audio/PDF assets by extension, and turns base64 or data-URL values into renderable data URLs or inline SVG text.

nodes.name: dataUrlFromMediaValue
nodes.summary: Converts an SDK media value (data URL, base64 payload, or SVG text) into a renderable data URL, normalizing the MIME type and percent-encoding SVGs when needed.

nodes.name: svgTextFromValue
nodes.summary: Extracts inline SVG markup from a media value by base64-decoding utf8 image/svg+xml content.

nodes.name: selection-bridge.ts
nodes.summary: Bridges raw DOM text selections to line-based comment ranges: formats labels, previews selected source lines, restores selections inside shadow roots, and exposes a gesture bridge for line-number click/drag selection.

nodes.name: lineInSelectedRange
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given line (and side) falls inside a selected range, normalizing inverted start/end and treating a null side as a match.

nodes.name: restoreShadowTextSelection
nodes.summary: Re-applies a DOM range inside a shadow root on the next animation frame so text selections survive re-renders.

nodes.name: createLineNumberSelectionBridge
nodes.summary: Creates a click/drag-to-select bridge over line-number gutters that tracks gesture state, consumes the resulting line range, and resets on mouseup or pointer leave.

nodes.name: virtualizer.ts
nodes.summary: Acquires and caches @pierre/diffs Virtualizer instances for the scroll container of each viewer, sharing one virtualizer per target element with setup and cleanup on acquire/release.

nodes.name: target
nodes.summary: Resolves the scroll container and virtualizer target element for a viewer, preferring the diffs scroller within the closest pierre host and falling back to computed scrollable ancestors.

nodes.name: acquireVirtualizer
nodes.summary: Returns a shared Virtualizer for the viewer's scroll target, setting it up on first acquire and returning a releaser that cleans it up when the last holder releases.

nodes.name: worker.ts
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and caches Shiki worker pools (unified and split styles) for syntax highlighting and word-diffs, sized at 2 workers per pool to bound memory and Safari worker startup cost.
nodes.languageNotes: The worker URL comes from a Vite `?worker&url` import of @pierre/diffs' Shiki worker; pools are module-level singletons keyed by diff style and guarded for SSR.

nodes.name: createPool
nodes.summary: Creates a WorkerPoolManager of two Shiki workers configured with the OpenCode theme and given line-diff type, initializing it eagerly.

nodes.name: getWorkerPool
nodes.summary: Returns the lazily-created worker pool for a diff style (unified or split), cached as module-level singletons and guarded against non-browser environments.

nodes.name: fixtures.ts
nodes.summary: Sample payloads (diff, code, markdown, changes) used as props by Storybook stories for the session-review and code views.

nodes.name: scaffold.tsx
nodes.summary: Storybook scaffolding factory: picks a component export from a module (by name, default, or first capitalized function), wraps it in an ErrorBoundary, and returns a CSF meta plus Basic story.

nodes.name: pick
nodes.summary: Selects a component from a module by explicit name, default export, or first capitalized function, falling back to a 'missing component' placeholder that lists the module's exports.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Builds a Storybook CSF object (meta + Basic story) for the picked component, rendering it via Dynamic inside an ErrorBoundary with a readable error fallback.

nodes.name: color.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free color math for the theme engine: hex/RGB/OKLCH conversions with gamut fitting, plus generators that expand seed colors into 12-step, neutral, and alpha scales for light and dark theme variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Scales are generated in the perceptual OKLab/OKLCH space (with sRGB linearization) so lightness steps stay visually even; fitOklch clamps out-of-gamut colors back into sRGB by reducing chroma.

nodes.name: hexToRgb
nodes.summary: Parses 3/4/6/8-digit hex color strings into RGB components, expanding short forms by doubling each digit.

nodes.name: rgbToOklch
nodes.summary: Converts sRGB to OKLCH via linearization and the OKLab transform, returning lightness, chroma, and hue in degrees.

nodes.name: oklchToRgb
nodes.summary: Converts OKLCH back to sRGB through the OKLab matrix, clamping out-of-range channels.

nodes.name: fitOklch
nodes.summary: Fits an OKLCH color into the displayable sRGB gamut by lowering lightness and chroma until the RGB conversion yields in-range channels, preserving hue.

nodes.name: generateScale
nodes.summary: Expands a seed hex color into a 12-step perceptual scale for light or dark themes, tilting lightness/hue/chroma across steps and capping chroma.

nodes.name: generateNeutralScale
nodes.summary: Generates the neutral (gray) scale from neutral and ink seed colors, mixing toward ink for contrast and enforcing monotonic lightness across the 12 steps.

nodes.name: generateAlphaScale
nodes.summary: Derives an alpha-variant scale by blending each step of a base scale toward transparency according to theme mode.

nodes.name: context.tsx
nodes.summary: SolidJS theme context: ThemeProvider/useTheme built on createSimpleContext, holding a reactive store of loaded themes plus persisted theme and color-scheme preferences (localStorage, cross-tab storage events, prefers-color-scheme) and a preview/commit/cancel flow for the theme picker.
nodes.languageNotes: Themes lazy-load via a Vite glob map (./themes/*.json) with in-flight promise dedup; the 'oc-2' theme is bundled as the synchronous default and preview state is stored separately from the committed themeId.

nodes.name: ThemeProvider
nodes.summary: SolidJS context provider (generated by createSimpleContext) whose init builds the reactive theme store, lazy theme loading, persistence and cross-tab sync, and the preview APIs; consumed through the paired useTheme hook.

nodes.name: default-themes.ts
nodes.summary: Re-exports the 38 built-in desktop themes (oc-2, catppuccin, gruvbox, tokyonight, ...) as typed DesktopTheme constants from their JSON files, plus the DEFAULT_THEMES registry.

nodes.name: desktop-theme.schema.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema (draft-07) for OpenCode desktop theme files: requires name, slug id, and light/dark variants, with definitions for HexColor, ColorValue (hex or var(--...) reference), legacy seed colors, and palettes.
nodes.languageNotes: ColorValue accepts either a hex color or a CSS variable reference, which is how themes can defer to runtime design tokens instead of hard-coding every color.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel for the theme runtime: re-exports color math, theme resolution/CSS application, ThemeProvider/useTheme, type definitions, and all built-in themes as the public UI theme API.
